intent: Keep the iteration-2 row (five 16 mm sensors at x = ±0.05 m, y = 0.04 m, mass 0.8 kg, body 0.12 by 0.18 m) and revert wheel_radius to 0.03 m, since 0.04 m scored worse. Change one thing: wheel_track from 0.12 m to 0.10 m, the untested narrower track the Integrator proposed. I expect max_error to move from 0.061 m, with line loss staying at zero, and I expect a score at or above about 26.99. I am considering, without committing, a wider sensor span (±0.07 m) if line loss returns with the narrower track, and I am not considering body or footprint changes, because the off-track limit is fixed at 0.06 m and footprint has shown no effect.
learning: Iteration 7 showed that a larger wheel (0.04 m) lowers progress slightly without moving max_error, so speed per wheel rotation is not the excursion. Track width is now the only untested steering-geometry lever. Ask the Integrator to report whether max_error moves at the start of the run or at a specific bend, and whether kp needs rescaling for the narrower track to avoid oscillation.
rationale: Iteration 7 tested wheel_radius 0.04 m against the iteration-2 row. It scored 26.6552, below the best 26.9949. Progress fell on the oval (0.1125 vs 0.115) and control effort rose, while max_error stayed at about 0.061 m. Larger wheels did not help, so I revert radius to 0.03 m. Across iterations 0 to 7, every run ended off_track with max_error of about 0.061 m. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), and no allowed body width raises it above 0.06 m, so the excursion sits just past a fixed limit. Span (±0.05 m) removed line loss, and footprint, mass, wheel_track 0.15 m, sensor y (0.02 to 0.06 m) and radius 0.04 m have not moved max_error. The one geometry lever not yet tested is a narrower wheel_track. The Integrator's contingency names wheel_track 0.10 m, and it was written for a 0.04 m radius, which has now been shown to be worse. I therefore apply it on the 0.03 m radius. A narrower track gives about 1.2 times more yaw per unit of wheel-speed difference (0.12/0.10), so the same steering command turns the robot harder. The Integrator may need to scale kp to keep the effective gain the same. That is their decision, and I do not set controller values here. Sensors (five 16 mm footprints at x = ±0.05 m, y = 0.04 m), mass 0.8 kg and body are unchanged, so the test isolates track width against the best-scoring row. Expected result: if the excursion is a steering-authority limit, max_error should move. I expect a modest change at most, and I do not expect runs to finish.
